decisions.executionNote: Begin a slow elbow-up approach with the left arm toward the purple nut. Keep the right arm parked; use the next view to refine position and wrist tilt.
Move over the purple nut, completing the downward wrist orientation while preserving elbow-up continuity. Stop above grasp height for visual alignment.
Correct the purple nut alignment using the wrist view and descend to the demonstrated grasp height, keeping the gripper open until alignment is checked.
Close around the centered purple nut and lift vertically. Retention will be checked from its position between the fingers, not the gripper command.
The purple nut remains between the fingers after lifting. Carry it above the matching purple bolt without crossing into the right workspace; refine the final alignment from the wrist image.
Lower the retained purple nut slowly toward the bolt axis, with a small lateral correction. Stop near initial engagement height before applying tightening rotation.
Center the purple shaft within the nut, then begin a small clockwise tightening turn with very shallow axial feed. Retention and engagement remain visually uncertain.
Pause rotation and correct the remaining purple bolt offset with a small planar motion, then lower only 2 mm. Check whether the shaft becomes centered in the nut.
The purple shaft is now centered in the aperture. Continue the clockwise turn by about one radian with a 1.2 mm feed, staying away from the wrist limit.
Release the seated purple nut and reset the wrist counterclockwise without translating. This prepares another tightening stroke while avoiding wrist overtravel.
Regrasp and tighten the purple nut by another controlled clockwise stroke. In parallel, begin the right arm's elbow-up approach to the gray nut, staying on its own side.
Reset the open left wrist for another tightening stroke; advance the right gripper above the gray nut and complete its downward orientation.
Apply another shallow clockwise purple-nut stroke. Lower the right hand toward the gray nut while correcting its position from the head calibration; keep that gripper open.
Open and reset the left wrist without undoing the purple nut. Close the right gripper around the centered gray nut and lift to verify retention before staging it at the middle.
Continue tightening purple with a shallow feed. The gray nut is visibly retained; carry it to the right edge of the shared middle staging area for a sequential handover.
Reset the released left wrist for another purple tightening stroke. Lower the gray nut onto the central staging area, keeping it closed until it is supported.
Tighten purple another stroke. Release the gray nut onto the table, then lift and withdraw the right hand from the middle so the left hand can retrieve it later.
Release the purple assembly and lift clear for a visual check, resetting the wrist only after opening. Move the right arm well out of the shared staging area.
The purple nut remains upright on its bolt after release. Bring the left hand above the staged gray nut at the middle, with the right hand parked well clear.
Descend the left open gripper onto the gray nut at the shared center staging point. The right hand remains withdrawn; check alignment before closing.
Close the left gripper on the centered gray nut and lift straight up. Verify that it remains between the fingers before moving toward its matching bolt.
The gray nut is retained in the left fingers. Carry it over the gray bolt in the left workspace, keeping clearance above the table before fine alignment.
Lower the held gray nut to initial bolt engagement height, making only a 2 mm lateral correction. Inspect shaft centering before tightening.
The gray shaft is offset to the right inside the nut. Correct that offset with a small planar motion and minimal descent before applying torque.
The gray shaft is now near the nut center. Begin a controlled clockwise stroke with a tiny residual lateral correction and shallow axial feed.
Pause the gray tightening stroke: the shaft is still off-center after rotation. Make a small planar correction toward the visible shaft, with only 1 mm descent, and recheck alignment.
The gray shaft is horizontally centered. Make a small correction along the remaining image direction and lower 3 mm to seat the nut before resuming tightening.
Finish a small gray-axis correction, release the nut in place, and reset the wrist for the next clockwise stroke. Keep the right arm clear.
The released gray nut has settled lower and appears coaxial with its bolt. Recenter and lower the open fingers to its new height, then regrasp and make a short tightening stroke.
Finish the gray tightening stroke, then open and reset the wrist while leaving the nut seated. The shaft remains centered in the nut.
Regrasp the seated gray nut and tighten another clockwise stroke with 2 mm of axial feed. Keep the bolt centered and the right hand parked.
Release the gray nut and reset the left wrist counterclockwise for another tightening stroke, keeping its position fixed and the right hand clear.
Regrasp the coaxial gray nut and apply another clockwise tightening stroke, feeding down only 1.5 mm. Keep both arms in their continuous elbow-up configurations.
Release the tightened gray nut and lift clear, resetting the wrist only with the gripper open. Check that the assembly remains upright before proceeding to red.
The gray assembly remains seated after release. Approach the red nut from the left at clearance height, preparing to stage it for the right arm without crossing the arms.
Lower the open left gripper to the red nut's grasp height, with a small calibrated planar adjustment. Keep the right arm withdrawn until the nut has been staged.
Use the left wrist view to center the red nut between the fingers, then close at the current height. Check the grasp before lifting or moving toward the middle.
Lift the centered red nut vertically before moving it to the shared middle staging area. Keep the gripper closed and the right hand withdrawn; inspect retention at the end.
The red nut is retained after lifting. Lower it onto the middle staging surface, then open only after reaching support height. Keep the right hand stationary until the left withdraws.
Lift the open left hand clear of the staged red nut, then withdraw into the left workspace. Only as it withdraws, advance the right hand partway toward the middle, keeping ample separation.
Bring the right gripper above the staged red nut while the left arm retracts toward its home orientation. Keep both elbows up and stop the right hand above grasp height for alignment.
Descend the open right gripper onto the red nut with a few millimeters of centering correction. Complete the left arm's return toward origin without crossing workspaces.
Close the right fingers around the red nut, then lift vertically to verify retention. Settle the open left arm at origin while keeping it clear of the handover area.
The red nut remains between the right fingers after lifting. Carry it above its matching bolt in the right workspace, maintaining clearance before alignment and descent.
Lower the retained red nut slowly toward initial engagement, correcting a small lateral offset seen in the wrist image. Inspect centering before tightening.
Correct the red nut toward the visibly left-offset shaft, with minimal axial motion and no rotation. Recheck coaxial alignment before tightening.
The red shaft is now centered inside the nut. Begin a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with only 2 mm axial feed, keeping the left arm open at origin.
Pause rotation to correct the red shaft offset revealed by the new wrist angle. Move a few millimeters toward the shaft and lower 1 mm before rechecking engagement.
The red shaft now appears centered. Release the nut to settle on the bolt and reset the open right wrist without translation, preparing another tightening stroke.
The released red nut has settled lower and appears coaxial. Recenter and lower the open fingers to that height, regrasp, then begin a short clockwise tightening stroke.
Continue the coaxial red nut's clockwise tightening stroke with shallow feed, then release in place. Stay within the wrist range and inspect seating before resetting.
Reset the open right wrist counterclockwise while the red nut stays seated. Keep the left gripper open at origin and preserve the elbow-up configuration.
Regrasp the seated red nut and tighten clockwise through another controlled stroke with only 1.5 mm axial feed. Keep the bolt centered and the left arm parked.
Release the seated red nut and reset the right wrist for another tightening stroke, holding position and keeping the left arm open at origin.
Regrasp and apply another clockwise red-nut stroke with a very shallow axial feed. The shaft is centered; keep the left gripper open at origin.
Release the red nut, lift the open hand clear, and reset the wrist. Check that the assembly remains seated before returning the right arm to origin.
The red nut remains seated after release. Retract the open right arm toward origin with a gradual wrist transition, preserving elbow-up continuity; settle the left home pose.
Complete the slow right-arm return to origin with both grippers open. Inspect the assemblies at rest; the purple nut may still need deeper tightening.
The purple nut shows more exposed internal thread than the other two. Reapproach it with the left arm for deeper tightening, keeping the right arm open at origin.
Complete the downward left-wrist orientation and approach the purple assembly with the gripper open. Check its settled height before regrasping for a final tightening pass.
Lower the open left fingers to the purple nut's settled height, recenter, then regrasp and begin a short tightening turn. Settle the open right arm at origin.
Continue tightening the centered purple nut with a 1.7-radian clockwise stroke and 2 mm feed, then release in place. Check depth before another stroke.
Reset the open left wrist while leaving the purple nut on its bolt. More internal thread is visible than on the other pairs, so prepare another shallow tightening pass.
Lower the open fingers 2 mm to the purple nut's settled height, regrasp, then tighten clockwise with a shallow axial feed. Keep the shaft centered and right arm at origin.
Release and reset the left wrist without translating the purple assembly. Its shaft remains centered, but several internal threads are visible, so recheck the settled nut before another pass.
Regrasp the centered purple nut and continue its clockwise tightening with a slow 4 mm axial feed over the stroke. Keep the right hand open and parked.
The purple nut is not visibly advancing and may sit above the finger contact. Release, raise 20 mm, and reset the wrist to re-establish a centered grasp on the nut rather than its shaft.
The purple nut is back near the finger contact region. Regrasp at this corrected height and apply a clockwise stroke with only 1.6 mm feed, checking that the nut advances rather than slipping.
Release the purple nut and reset the open wrist at the corrected grasp height. The nut remains coaxial, but its visible depth still needs confirmation before returning home.
Regrasp the purple nut at the corrected height and tighten another clockwise stroke with 2.5 mm axial feed. Inspect its depth after release rather than relying on gripper state.
Release the purple nut and reset the wrist through a wider but continuous arc, preparing another tightening stroke. Keep the assembly undisturbed and the right arm parked.
Regrasp the coaxial purple nut and tighten through the prepared clockwise arc, feeding down only 2.3 mm. Keep the right arm open at origin and check visible depth afterward.
Release the purple nut and reset the left wrist without translation. The shaft remains centered and appears deeper; prepare one more controlled tightening stroke while settling the right home pose.
Regrasp the centered purple nut and apply another controlled clockwise stroke with 2.4 mm feed. Keep the right arm open at origin; verify depth after release.
Release the purple nut and reset the open left wrist without translation. Its shaft appears deeper in the aperture; prepare another shallow tightening stroke.
Regrasp the seated purple nut and tighten through the prepared clockwise arc with 2.4 mm axial feed. Maintain alignment and keep the right arm open at origin.
